{{Short description|Finger counting method}}
[[File:Chisanbop hands numbered.jpg|thumb|upright=1.3|The Chisanbop system. When a finger is touching the table, it contributes its corresponding number to a total.]]
'''Chisanbop''' or '''chisenbop''' (from Korean ''chi (ji)'' finger + ''sanpŏp (sanbeop)'' calculation <ref>chisanbop. (n.d.). Dictionary.com Unabridged (v 1.1). Retrieved June 29, 2007, from Dictionary.com website: http://dictionary.reference.com/browse/chisanbop</ref> 지산법/指算法), sometimes called '''Fingermath''',<ref>{{cite book
|author = Lieberthal, Edwin M
|year = 1979
|title = The Complete Book of Fingermath: Simple, Accurate, Scientific
|url = https://archive.org/details/completebookoffi0000lieb
|url-access = registration
|publisher = London : Souvenir Press
|isbn = 0285624385}}
</ref> is a [[finger counting]] method used to perform basic [[math]]ematical operations.  According to ''The Complete Book of Chisanbop''<ref>{{cite book
|author = Pai, Hang Young 
|year = 1981
|title = The Complete Book of Chisanbop: Original Finger Calculation Method Created by Sung Jin Pai and Hang Young Pai
|url = https://archive.org/details/completebookofch00paih
|url-access = registration
|publisher = Van Nostrand Reinhold
|isbn = 0-442-27568-4}}</ref> 
by Hang Young Pai, chisanbop was created in the 1940s in [[Korea]] by Sung Jin Pai and revised by his son Hang Young Pai, who brought the system to the [[United States]] in 1977.

With the ''chisanbop'' method, it is possible to represent all numbers from 0 to 99 with the hands, rather than the usual 0 to 10, and to add, subtract, multiply and divide numbers.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Casebeer |first1=William D. |title=Natural Ethical Facts: Evolution, Connectionism and Moral Cognition |date=2001 |publisher=University of California, San Diego |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=7egSAtSdpcgC&pg=PA146 |access-date=7 November 2019 |language=en}}</ref> The system has been described as being easier to use than a physical abacus for students with visual impairments.<ref>{{cite journal |journal=Education of the Visually Handicapped |date=1979 |volume=11-12 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=E84cAQAAMAAJ |access-date=7 November 2019 |publisher=Association for Education of the Visually Handicapped |language=en |title=Education of the Visually Handicapped: The Official Publication of Association for Education of the Visually Handicapped }}</ref>

== Basic concepts ==

[[File:Chisanbop fingers pressed (36).jpg|thumb|36 represented in chisanbop, where four fingers and a thumb are touching the table and the rest of the digits are raised. The three fingers on the left hand represent 10+10+10 = 30; the thumb and one finger on the right hand represent 5+1=6.]]

[[File:Counting from 1 to 20 in Chisenbop.webm|thumb|Counting from 1 to 20 in Chisanbop]]

Each finger has a value of one, while the thumb has a value of five. Therefore, each hand can represent the digits 0–9, rather than the usual 0–5.

The two hands combine to represent two digits; the right hand is the ones place, and the left hand is the tens place. This way, any number from 0 to 99 can be shown, and it's possible to count up to 99 instead of just 10.

The hands can be held above a table, with the fingers pressing down on the table; or the hands can simply be held up, fingers extended, as with the more common practice of 0-10 counting.
<ref>
{{cite book
|author = Pai, Hang Young 
|year = 1981
|title = The Complete book of Chisanbop, 1981 (pages from 2 to 19)
|url = http://archive.computerhistory.org/resources/access/text/2010/03/500004045.05.01.acc.pdf
|url-access = registration
|publisher = Van Nostrand Reinhold

}}</ref>

== Adoption in the United States ==
Chisanbop can be used for teaching math, or simply for counting. The results for teaching math have been mixed. A school in [[Shawnee Mission, Kansas]], ran a pilot program with students in 1979. It was found that although they could add large numbers quickly, they could not add them in their heads. The program was dropped. Grace Burton of the [[University of North Carolina]] said, "It doesn't teach the basic number facts, only to count faster. Adding and subtracting quickly are only a small part of mathematics."<ref>{{Cite journal | url=https://www.csmonitor.com/1982/0517/051703.html |title = What about Chisanbop -- who's using it?|journal = Christian Science Monitor|date = 1982-05-17}}</ref>
